title: The Battle of the Century at Roseland: Henderson against Goldkette
summary: The Goldkette band opposed Henderson during Carter's stint, and he recalls Bill Challis's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When you replaced Don Redmond [phonetic] for that brief period with Fletcher Henderson, that happened, oddly enough, to be at a very major event, which in retrospect has been blown up to be a very major event, but you may not recall it as such. It was billed as, at Roseland, the Battle of the Century, another one of these battles. When Gene Goldcat’s [phonetic] band . . .
Was that during the time I was with him?
Oh, yeah, I guess so, because I remember the Goldcat Band from that.

So that was one of the premier encounters, I guess, in jazz history, was that night, and that happened to be during the period you were replacing Don Redmond. Any details of that event come to mind after all this time?
My greatest impression as of this moment was . . . oh, boy, one of the arrangements.
Their arrangements. What’s the arranger’s name, anyway?

Bill Chalice, yes, yes. Some excellent arrangements, I thought. I was very impressed with that, yes. And, of course, I was very impressed with the Charlie Dixon [phonetic] arrangements and the Don Redmond arrangements, which I was . . .
